transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As you know from the quarterly review context, we're looking to reduce avoidable cloud spend on the production video-transcoding cluster in us-east-2 without changing its ownership or region. The current draft policy proposes a peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes, one shared pool for all customers, 30 days of standard logs, and cross-region archival to us-west-2. Before I make a final decision, our standing cost-review routine requires reliability, security, support, and FinOps to each confirm their operational constraints. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you — please share any concerns or constraints related to this draft policy so we can address them before publishing.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical reliability constraint. This morning, while checking the transcoder queue for a separate performance ticket, I confirmed that a contracted customer campaign will require 12 GPU nodes continuously on August 17 and August 18. The campaign booking was finalized in the customer system just minutes ago and hasn't yet been copied into the infrastructure cost-review document. The proposed peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes would be insufficient for those dates and would cause a production capacity failure for a contracted commitment.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a security constraint to flag. During an unrelated access-log audit yesterday, I confirmed that production transcoding access logs must be retained for exactly 90 days in an immutable archive. The draft policy's proposal of 30 days of standard logs would violate this requirement. I'm still waiting for the security ticket number before adding this requirement to the review document, but the 90-day immutable retention is a hard constraint that needs to be reflected in the published policy.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a support constraint to flag. I confirmed with the account team this afternoon that the enterprise customer Orchid has a 15-minute queue-latency SLA and must have 2 dedicated GPU nodes excluded from shared-pool scale-down. The account note was updated after the draft policy circulated and has not yet been reflected in the infrastructure proposal. This means the proposed single shared pool for all customers would put Orchid's SLA at risk, since those 2 dedicated nodes need to be carved out and protected from scale-down.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a FinOps constraint to flag. While reconciling the last cloud invoice, I found that the proposed cross-region archival to us-west-2 would create a recurring cross-region egress charge of approximately $4,000 per month. The invoice investigation is still open, so I haven't yet amended the cost model, but this is a significant cost impact that needs to be factored into the policy decision before publishing.

commitments.detail: Peak GPU node allowance raised from 6 to 12 to cover the contracted customer campaign on August 17-18. Mateo to add the finalized campaign booking to the infrastructure cost-review document.
Log retention extended from 30 to 90 days in an immutable archive. Nia to add the security ticket number to the review document once received.

2 dedicated GPU nodes carved out for enterprise customer Orchid, excluded from shared-pool scale-down to protect the 15-minute queue-latency SLA. Harper to ensure the account note is reflected in the updated policy.

Cross-region archival to us-west-2 replaced with same-region (us-east-2) archival to eliminate the ~$4,000/month cross-region egress charge. Theo to update the cost model once the invoice investigation closes.
